slides.title: Welcome to Understanding APIs
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on Understanding APIs.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn,

• Define what an **API** is in the context of **AI**.
• Explain the role of **API** keys in secure **API** access.
• Describe how applications send requests and receive **AI**-generated responses.
• Apply the concept of **prompts** as inputs for **AI** models.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration: Here I am using a browser on a computer or mobile.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration: To follow this tutorial, you should have basics of **Python**.

slides.title: What is an API? Think of it like...
slides.narration:
What if I told you different software applications can talk to each other?
Imagine you are at a restaurant.
You tell the waiter your order.
The waiter takes your order to the kitchen.
The kitchen prepares your food.
Then, the waiter brings your food back to you.
Here, the waiter is like an **API**.
An **API**, or **Application Programming Interface**, is a software intermediary.
It allows two applications to communicate.
It takes your request and delivers the response.
With that understanding, let's see how **APIs** work with **AI** models.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing API with simple icons, connecting two applications

slides.title: Prompts as Inputs to AI Models
slides.narration:
How do you tell an **AI** model what you want it to do?
You send it a **prompt**.
A **prompt** is your instruction or question.
It is the input you give to the **AI** model.
You send these **prompts** through an **API**.
For example, you might **prompt** an **AI** to 'Write a short story about a talking cat.'
The **API** delivers this **prompt** to the **AI** model.
But how do we ensure only authorized users send these **prompts**?
slides.image_prompt: Person at laptop, typing a prompt like 'Write a short story about a talking cat.'

slides.title: API Keys: Your Digital Credentials
slides.narration:
To keep **APIs** secure, we use **API** keys.
Think of an **API** key as your digital credential.
It is a unique code.
You send this key with your request.
**API** keys authenticate your requests.
They control your access to **API** services.
This ensures only authorized users can interact with the **AI**.
Just like a hotel key card lets you enter your room.
Your **API** key grants you access to the **API**.
Now, let's look at how applications actually send these requests.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a digital key or a key card unlocking a service

slides.title: Comparing Request Methods
slides.narration:

Now, look at the improved request on the right.
The vague request gives the **AI** little direction.
The improved request gives clear, specific instructions.

Clear **prompts** save time and improve accuracy.

Let us summarize what we learned today.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We defined **APIs** as intermediaries for applications.
We saw how **prompts** are inputs for **AI** models.
**API** keys secure access to **API** services.
Finally, we learned to send effective requests to **AI**.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now as an assignment,
Create a simple **Python** script to send a basic text **prompt** to an **AI** model using a hypothetical **API**.
Ensure your **prompt** is clear and specific.
Compare the results of a vague versus a specific **prompt**.
